head: c455b9c
task: P16.10b Task 3 — production Proto creation ownership inventory
purpose: Grep-audit of EVERY production Proto creation path. Drives the ProtoTreeOwner design (Tasks 4-9) from actual creation sites, not hypotheticals. Verified by reading each call site; file:line refer to c455b9c.
method: All Proto allocations funnel through exactly two constructors: bc.ProtoBuilder.finish() (text compiler) and undump.UndumpReader.undumpProto() (binary loader). Every caller of those two was traced to its Lua/CLI/C-API trigger, its allocator, and its error paths. OP_CLOSURE creates NO new Proto (shares an existing tree node). string.dump creates NO Proto since P16.10b T1 (DumpOptions.strip).

sites.creation: one heap Proto per function; children finish() first (compileChildFunction:4630), then parent adopts via addProto; root returned
sites.allocator: the Codegen's allocator == its caller's allocator (see S1a-S1d)
sites.tree_shape: root + recursive children via proto.p; acyclic by construction (children never reference parents)
sites.keeps_alive_today: NOTHING. gcFreeObject(.closure) (vm.zig:21996) frees upvalues + struct only; the 'Closure owns the Proto' comments (vm.zig:23312-23316, 23596-23597) are FALSE — no production code path ever frees a Proto. Proto.deinit is called only from unit tests (bytecode.zig:845,869; codegen_bc.zig:6931..7379).
sites.releases_today: none -> repeated load() grows linearly (lane repeated_dynamic_load: ~2333 MB/decade)
sites.error_before_closure: compile error after some children finished: finished children sit in Codegen.builder.protos; Codegen.deinit (codegen_bc.zig:575) frees only the builder's ArrayList storage, NOT the finished Proto trees -> partial-tree leak on error. Callers then return error.Syntax; no closure exists, nobody owns the orphans.

sites.trigger: Lua load(text), loadfile, dofile; the ONLY path for dynamic text loads in the CLI
sites.keeps_alive_extra: Vm.pinned_source_strings pins the source LuaString forever (vm.zig:23626) because compiled protos borrow lexeme slices (locvar names, upvalue names, function name, source_name when default) from the source bytes; compileChunkValue callers additionally pass caller-owned buffers (see S2)
sites.notes: load(reader-fn) collects pieces into source_owned heap slice (vm.zig:23519) that is NEVER freed (leak) and IS borrowed by the tree; shebang chunks build prefixed_owned heap slice (vm.zig:23533) likewise never freed and borrowed. Both are un-pinned hazards/leaks the tree owner must absorb.

sites.notes: owner must take a copy of name+bytes for this path (no GC object exists to retain)

sites.creation: NO new Proto. closure.proto = parent_tree.p[b] — the child proto is SHARED: many closures may reference one child, and child closures routinely outlive the root closure (returning nested functions is idiomatic)
sites.sharing_verdict: SUPPORTED sharing, not theoretical: every Lua program returning an inner function exercises parent-dies-child-lives. Any ownership model MUST keep the tree alive while ANY closure of ANY node lives.
sites.release_implication: freeing the tree when the ROOT closure dies (naive 'closure owns proto') is incorrect; gcFreeObject(.closure) must release a per-TREE reference, not free a per-closure proto

cross_vm_sharing.evidence: every text compile and every undump happens inside exactly one Vm (compiler callback and undump intern callback both close over self: *Vm); the CLI runs a single Vm per process; c_api suites create a fresh Vm per test and load fresh chunks into it. No production path hands a Proto tree to a second Vm.
cross_vm_sharing.implication_for_task_8: runtime trees are one-VM-bound in practice -> VM-interned constants living in the tree are legitimate; enforce with a Debug assert (owner.vm == executing vm) at the execution boundary rather than runtime machinery.

text_compiled_tree_borrows: proto.locvars[*].name, proto.upvalues[*].name, proto.name — lexeme slices into the SOURCE BYTES (codegen slices ast spans against self.source)
proto.source_name — chunk name bytes: either the source string itself (default), a distinct caller name string (load(s, name)), or caller memory (compileChunkValue/S1b)
undumped_tree_borrows: non-fixed: name slices alias the chunk buffer -> currently duped by cloneUndumpedStrings (self-contained)
fixed ('B'): code/lineinfo arrays conceptually + ALL name slices + long-string constants (external LuaStrings) alias the chunk buffer -> currently VM-pinned forever
resolution_state_borrows: post-resolution k.str entries are VM-interned (owned by VM string table); pre-resolution they are seed-0 LuaStrings owned by the tree (Proto.deinit's constants_resolved hack encodes exactly this ambiguity per-proto)

gc_accounting_today.charged: Closure struct+upvalue-ptrs (gcNoteAlloc at 11711/14751/23015/23336), Cells, strings interned at resolution
gc_accounting_today.not_charged: ALL Proto-tree memory (structs, code, k, p, lineinfo, locvars, live_reg_top, resolved_values, cloneUndumpedStrings dupes) and the pinned source strings' extra retention is charged only via their original string alloc
gc_accounting_today.result: collectgarbage('count') under-reports by every live chunk's tree size; gcNoteFree in gcFreeObject(.closure) credits only the Closure — balanced but blind to trees

design_conclusions: C1: A per-TREE refcounted owner is the smallest clean fit: sharing is per-tree (S5), roots die before children (S5), and exactly two construction sites (S1, S2) plus one VM-bind site (S3) must create it. VM-global retention is wrong (a long-lived VM must collect dead chunks) and no site needs cross-VM sharing (cross_vm_sharing).

C2: Owner must absorb source backing: retained LuaString refs for load(string)/fixed-undump, owned heap copies for reader-fn buffers, prefixed buffers, and compileChunkValue caller memory (S1a/S1b/S2). This retires Vm.pinned_source_strings entirely.

C3: k-string ownership must become structural: provenance (text-compiled vs undumped) + a single atomic tree-wide 'adopted' flip on the owner — replacing per-proto constants_resolved and fixing the latent re-resolution destroy-VM-string OOM bug in resolveProtoConstants (intern fallible AFTER in-place destroys).

C4: Error paths to fix while introducing the owner: Codegen.deinit must free finished-but-unclaimed protos (S1); undumpProto needs errdefer partial-tree cleanup (S2); closure-alloc failure after compile must release the tree (Tasks 13).
C5: Charge tree bytes to the VM when the tree is bound to it (all load paths + CLI runBytecode bind with the same allocator family today); credit on last release. resolved_values charged when built.
